title: Claude runtime adapter
description: Objective: implement the Foundation Claude capability probe and runtime adapter contract. Deliverable: focused runner provider modules plus development-only golden streams for complete, crash, truncate, reorder, cancel, and version-change cases. NOT in scope: Codex, billing assumptions, automatic authority, or provider resume unless capability-proven. Hard dependency: Runtime contract registry. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/providers/claude/** and packages/testkit/src/providers/claude/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test.
definitionOfDone: Probe records an immutable runtime closure and returns typed UNSUPPORTED for every unproven capability.
Structured and raw events preserve exact order/bytes and bind the stable Moe effect identity.
Cancellation, crash, truncation, reordering, and runtime drift reconcile to proven result or honest UNKNOWN.
The focused runner typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

THREE judgement calls worth QA's attention, each with a test:
1. The closure is SORTED BY PATH before hashing. Discovery order is not a fact about the runtime, and letting it into the digest would make the wrapper's pre-`effect.activate` comparison (design 13) report drift that never happened. Test builds the same closure forward and reversed and asserts one digest. Duplicate paths are refused (CLAUDE_OBSERVATION_CLOSURE_DUPLICATE) rather than silently deduped — one runtime file counted twice is a broken observation, not a tidy-up.
2. truthClass is deliberately INDEPENDENT of pinningMethod. PROVEN = at least one digested closure member AND a self-reported version. A runtime that is honestly observed but cannot be pinned is still honestly observed — it just cannot launch authoritatively. That second question is the separate exported predicate `runtimePinningIsAuthoritative(o)` = PROVEN && pinningMethod !== UNSUPPORTED, which is a READ over the record: it grants nothing and starts nothing (design 13 gives pinning EXECUTION to the wrapper/supervisor).
3. `observationDigestInput` is exported and takes `Omit<ProviderRuntimeObservation,"observationDigest">`, so the digest provably cannot cover itself and a stored observation can be re-verified without reconstructing the field list. A test asserts the digest string does not appear inside its own input.

Capability probe. Split across claude-capabilities.ts (289: vocabulary + proof rules) and claude-probe.ts (120: orchestration + observation binding) — this is the plan's own step-6 split point, taken now rather than at the gate because the single file had reached 364 lines against a 400 hard bound. claude-probe.ts re-exports the vocabulary so the module's public surface is unchanged.

CLOSED 11-member vocabulary, all present on every probe, vocabulary-ordered: CANCEL_ON_READING, CONTEXT_LIMIT_DECLARATION, PIN_METHOD, PROCESS_TREE_TERMINATION, RAW_STREAM, RESUME, RUN_ENUMERATION_NEGATIVE_PROOF, SCHEMA_VERSION_REPORT, STRUCTURED_STREAM, TOKENIZER_AVAILABILITY, VERSION_REPORT. Status vocabulary is two-valued SUPPORTED|UNSUPPORTED — unproven is UNSUPPORTED, never absent, never optimistic.

THE DESIGN-864 RECONCILIATION (the plan said capability UNKNOWN in one clause and "every unproven capability = UNSUPPORTED" in another; both are honored without a third status): CONTEXT_LIMIT_DECLARATION is UNSUPPORTED when unproven, AND the profile separately carries `contextLimit: {kind: EXACT_TOKENS|CONSERVATIVE_INPUT_BYTES|UNKNOWN}` plus `contextPolicy: ADMISSIBLE|HOLD_UNKNOWN`. "The capability is not proven" and "policy must hold" are two different statements and the record makes both. Tested across null / explicit UNKNOWN / zero tokens / negative bytes -> UNKNOWN + HOLD_UNKNOWN, and a valid 1 MiB conservative byte bound -> ADMISSIBLE.

PROOF IS OBSERVATION, NOT CLAIM — this is the part that defeats capability laundering. The port hands over observation records, not booleans, and a record that contradicts its own claim proves the OPPOSITE: processTreeObservation with childrenAfter > 0 -> PROCESS_TREE_TERMINATION UNSUPPORTED; cancelObservation whose terminatedAtSequence precedes requestedAtSequence -> CANCEL_ON_READING UNSUPPORTED; runEnumeration whose "provenAbsentRunId" appears in enumeratedRunIds -> UNSUPPORTED; structuredSample that does not parse to a JSON object -> UNSUPPORTED; tokenizer reporting 0 tokens -> UNSUPPORTED. Each has its own assertion. `helpText` is carried for diagnostics and proves nothing: a report containing "--output-format stream-json --max-tokens --resume --kill-tree --list-sessions" and no observations yields all-11-UNSUPPORTED + HOLD_UNKNOWN + truthClass UNKNOWN. RESUME is hard-pinned UNSUPPORTED with proofMethod NONE even when the port supplies a resumeClaim (design 21.1 "help text is not capability proof", 21.4 runtime-pinned Claude only). An invariant assertion sweeps all 11 records: SUPPORTED implies a proofMethod other than NONE, UNSUPPORTED implies exactly NONE — so no record can be SUPPORTED without naming what proved it.

implementationPlan.description: Testkit golden streams — packages/testkit/src/providers/claude/claude-golden-streams.ts + claude-golden-streams.test.ts. Fixture corpus per the design's FULL closed list (684, not the six-item sketch): complete, cancelled, crashed, DUPLICATED, reordered, MALFORMED, truncated, RESUMED (expressed as the typed-UNSUPPORTED refusal fixture — resume discontinuity present, adapter must refuse since RESUME is UNSUPPORTED), version-mismatched. Every raw payload BASE64-ENCODED inside the module (MANDATORY: .gitattributes line 1 `* text=auto eol=lf` silently normalizes CRLF in committed text files — a raw Windows CLI stream containing \r\n would be corrupted and its pinned digest would never match; base64 is the only representation needing no .gitattributes edit); every fixture labeled DEVELOPMENT_ONLY + NOT_CONFIRMATORY with pinned sha256 via testkit's landed canonicalize/identifyEvidence. claude-golden-streams.test.ts (in-package relative imports — legal): digest-pin stability (two builds byte-identical), label presence, corpus completeness vs the design-684 list (mechanical set equality), base64 round-trip byte fidelity incl. a fixture containing literal \r\n bytes. Runs under both the testkit filter and root vitest.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD red then green. RED: test written first, failed at import (`Cannot find module './claude-golden-streams.js'`, "no tests"). Second RED was the digest pin — the module shipped a zeroed CLAUDE_GOLDEN_CORPUS_DIGEST and the suite reported the real value, which was then pinned. GREEN: `pnpm exec vitest run --root . packages/testkit/src/providers` -> 1 file / 7 passed; `pnpm --filter @moe/testkit typecheck` -> exit 0. 262 production + 110 test lines.

CORPUS — exactly the closed design-11.5 list, nine cases, no more and no fewer: cancelled, complete, crashed, duplicated, malformed, reordered, resumed, truncated, version-mismatched. Completeness is asserted against a list written out LONGHAND IN THE TEST, not derived from the module — a corpus that defines its own completeness target can never fail that assertion. Case-set equality is mechanical (sorted array compare) plus a length check, and the module additionally refuses at load if the parsed cases do not cover the closed list exactly once.

Each fixture is a JSON-lines provider stream carrying schemaVersion + monotonic seq + type, so the runner-side anomaly detector has something real to detect: crashed ends after a mid-run record with NO terminal result; duplicated repeats seq 2 byte-identically; reordered delivers seq 3 before seq 2; malformed carries a broken JSON line that still ends in a newline (distinguishing "bad record" from "cut stream"); truncated ends mid-object with NO trailing newline; resumed OPENS at seq 7 with resumedFrom set (the resume-discontinuity the adapter must refuse, since RESUME is UNSUPPORTED); version-mismatched starts on claude-stream-json/1 and switches to /2 mid-stream, which is the unknown-schema case that must land in the UNKNOWN family rather than the wrapper's PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED.

Fixture bytes are synthetic and labeled as such. Every entry carries label DEVELOPMENT_ONLY and confirmatory NOT_CONFIRMATORY, asserted per case; the module header states plainly that nothing here may be cited as proof of a provider capability (design Phase 1).

CRLF IS A TESTED PROPERTY, NOT A COMMENT. `complete` is authored with real \r\n line endings, and the test scans the decoded bytes for 0x0D 0x0A pairs and asserts exactly 3, while `cancelled` is asserted to contain no 0x0D at all. That is the direct guard against `.gitattributes` `* text=auto eol=lf`, which would silently normalise a committed raw text fixture and break its pin. Base64 is what makes the fixture inert under that normalisation.

INTERCHANGE CONTRACT for step 4 (runner cannot import this package — rootDir:"src" fails its own gate). The corpus is ONE JSON document in a template literal delimited by `moe-claude-golden-corpus/1 DATA BEGIN` / `... DATA END` marker comments, both also exported as string constants. A test asserts each marker appears exactly twice in the module's own source (once as the exported constant, once as the delimiter), then performs the SAME extraction a foreign reader will perform — lastIndexOf both markers, slice, JSON.parse — and checks the parsed version and case count. So the extraction rule is exercised from the producing side before step 4 depends on it.

The per-case `sha256` is over the RAW DECODED BYTES, deliberately NOT over canonical JSON. That keeps runner and testkit from having to agree on a canonicalizer implementation to verify a fixture — a cross-package gate resting on two independent canonicalizers agreeing byte-for-byte would be a latent trap. A foreign reader needs only sha256. Corpus-level stability is a separate concern and stays in-package: claudeGoldenCorpusIdentity() uses testkit's landed identifyCanonicalEvidence and is pinned to fadd4d913de06fb49723ffe2cfb3b713175b75a164531207daa5e53b43a5b8a3, so any fixture edit must update that constant in the same commit.

Validation runs at module load and THROWS: unsupported corpus version, malformed case, unknown case id, non-sha256 digest, base64 that does not re-encode identically, declared byteLength disagreeing with the decode, or a digest mismatch. A drifted fixture fails loudly on first import instead of quietly handing out bytes that no longer match their pin. claudeGoldenStreamBytes returns a FRESH copy per call so a consumer cannot mutate the shared corpus, and an unknown case id throws rather than returning an empty stream (asserted).

Scope note: packages/testkit/src/index.ts was NOT touched — it is outside this task's owned paths. Consequence, deliberate and checked: the corpus is not part of the testkit public entrypoint, so the foundation raw-node entrypoint smoke worker never loads it and no `.js` shim is required here (see the @moe/skills handoff, which flagged shims as the trap for the first raw-node importer).

FIXTURE CONSUMPTION — the interchange contract from step 3 works end to end. The test fs-reads packages/testkit/src/providers/claude/claude-golden-streams.ts via `new URL("../../../../../packages/testkit/...", import.meta.url)`, slices the marker-delimited block, JSON.parses it, and for EVERY case re-verifies `sha256Hex(decoded) === declared sha256` AND `decoded.byteLength === declared byteLength` at module load, throwing before any test body runs. A fixture that drifted by one byte fails loudly here rather than silently changing what these tests mean (this is what step 7(c) will probe by flipping a byte). Zero cross-package imports; runner typecheck stays clean.

DISPOSITION MATRIX — all nine golden cases driven to an exact typed outcome, asserted with caseId-prefixed strings so a failure names the case: complete -> COMPLETED []; cancelled -> CANCELLED []; crashed -> INCOMPLETE []; duplicated -> COMPLETED [DUPLICATE_EVENT]; reordered -> COMPLETED [OUT_OF_ORDER]; malformed -> UNKNOWN [MALFORMED_RECORD]; truncated -> UNKNOWN [TRUNCATION]; resumed -> REFUSED_RESUME_UNSUPPORTED [RESUME_DISCONTINUITY]; version-mismatched -> UNKNOWN_SCHEMA [UNKNOWN_SCHEMA_VERSION].

Precedence is explicit and documented, strongest first: RESUME_DISCONTINUITY -> REFUSED_RESUME_UNSUPPORTED (v1 refuses a resumed stream outright, since RESUME is UNSUPPORTED); UNKNOWN_SCHEMA_VERSION -> UNKNOWN_SCHEMA; any DESTRUCTIVE anomaly (GAP, COUNTER_REGRESSION, MALFORMED_RECORD, TRUNCATION) -> UNKNOWN; only then may a terminal `result` record speak, cancelled subtype -> CANCELLED else COMPLETED; otherwise INCOMPLETE. DUPLICATE_EVENT and OUT_OF_ORDER are deliberately NON-destructive: a byte-identical redelivery and a late arrival both leave the full evidence intact, so downgrading them to UNKNOWN would manufacture doubt. UNKNOWN_SCHEMA is a distinct disposition from the wrapper's PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED and a test asserts that string appears nowhere in a serialized record — the two failure points stay distinguishable.

THREE DETECTION SUBTLETIES that a naive record-by-record scanner gets wrong; each is documented in-source and pinned by a test:
1. GAP is computed over the SET of observed sequences, not delivery order. Out-of-order delivery looks exactly like a gap followed by a late arrival, so per-record judging would report a hole the next record fills — the `reordered` fixture (1,3,2,4) would falsely raise GAP. Set analysis: span = max-min+1 compared against distinct count + malformed count.
2. A malformed record still OCCUPIED a slot, so it counts toward that comparison and advances the expected counter. Otherwise the `malformed` fixture (1, unreadable, 3) invents a GAP for a record that was delivered and merely unreadable.
3. COUNTER_REGRESSION suppresses gap analysis entirely — across a counter restart, contiguity is undefined, so guessing it would be noise. COUNTER_REGRESSION (a sequence at or below the stream's ORIGIN) is separated from OUT_OF_ORDER (a sequence below the previous one but still above the origin); dedicated test drives 5,6,1 -> [COUNTER_REGRESSION] and 1,3,2 -> [OUT_OF_ORDER]. The first record establishes the origin and is never gap-checked: the adapter does not know what sequence number a provider starts at, and assuming 1 would flag every resumed or offset stream. RESUME_DISCONTINUITY therefore keys on an explicit `resumedFrom` declaration, NOT on "first seq != 1".

ORDER AND BYTE PRESERVATION (DoD 2), asserted directly: events keep DELIVERY order, never sorted by declared sequence — the reordered fixture yields declaredSequence [1,3,2,4] against ordinals [0,1,2,3]. Framing splits on \n and strips one trailing \r, so a Windows CRLF capture yields the same records as a POSIX one while the raw bytes stay untouched for the digest; the test reconstructs the entire `complete` fixture by rejoining event payloads with \r\n and comparing to the original text, and asserts each event's lineSha256 matches a fresh sha256Hex of its bytes and that no retained line contains a stray 0x0D. A cut trailing segment is TRUNCATION and is deliberately NOT emitted as an event — emitting a half-written line would let a partial record be read as content (the `truncated` fixture reports only TRUNCATION, never MALFORMED_RECORD). The malformed line IS emitted, with declaredSequence and type null, so it is recorded without pretending it parsed.

comments.content: Roadmap amendment 2026-08-07: the Claude adapter must consume the provider-neutral validated skill snapshot from task-eca1a82ffa844c679d25a60ad8bd165e and the durable project instruction contract from task-02249f0a600247a6977949648ec64886. Rendering must be deterministic, capability-probed, digest-recorded, and unable to convert advisory text into command/effect authority.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 10 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Runner tests relative-importing testkit TS — REJECTED, empirically proven fatal: composite:true + rootDir:'src' -> TS6307 under the task's own typecheck gate (the tests/property loophole exists only because root tests/ have no tsconfig). Resolution: golden streams committed as base64 data in testkit (owned path), runner tests fs-READ via new URL + import.meta.url (package-boundary.test.ts precedent) and re-verify pinned digests with runner's landed sha256Hex before use. (2) @moe/testkit devDependency — REJECTED: three+ touches outside owned paths (runner package.json, lockfile, testkit index exports — exports map blocks deep subpaths) and would make runner the precedent-setting first testkit dependent; junction experiments proved it CAN work but the scope cost is unjustified. (3) @moe/skills dependency for the renderer input type — REJECTED: structural local mirror with literal types (advisoryOnly:true, authority:'NONE') + pinned 'moe-skill-renderer-input/1' version literal; scheduler zero-dep precedent; the amendment mandates consuming the snapshot, not a dep; drift guarded by version-literal rejection. (4) Thin observation shape — REJECTED (BLOCKER): design 221 mandates the full closure/pinning-method/platform/freshness/truth shape so the wrapper's pre-activate comparison (798) is decidable; pinning EXECUTION stays with the supervisor. (5) Resume as tentative 'resume?' — REJECTED: definite vocabulary member, typed UNSUPPORTED in v1 (1304/1322); the RESUMED golden fixture asserts the refusal. (6) Raw bytes verbatim unbounded — REJECTED: digest coverage unbounded, inline retention bounded 16MiB+64KiB tail with artifact-ref overflow (1135). (7) PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED for mid-stream drift — REJECTED: that code is the wrapper's pre-activation refusal; mid-stream unknown schema -> UNKNOWN family (684), keeping the two failure points distinguishable. Verified by 2-agent workflow (design-boundary + mechanics with junction/TS6307 experiments); 3 BLOCKERs + 5 RISKs folded in.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Design anchors: 221 (full ProviderRuntimeObservation field list; digest binds quote/attempt/launch-intent), 648/672 (adapter contract incl. quote/doctor — deferred, layout must not preclude AdmissionQuote), 676-684 (capability declaration list; closed anomaly list; golden corpus list: complete/cancelled/crashed/duplicated/reordered/malformed/truncated/resumed/version-mismatched; raw preserved BY DIGEST; unknown schema -> UNKNOWN), 798 (wrapper owns pre-activate compare + pinning execution + lock/credential/adoption/SUSPECT), 864/876 (context-limit declaration; CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE; conservative byte bound + token UNKNOWN), 872-874/257 (providerInputDigest distinct from contextDigest; envelope version in digest), 1135 (16MiB+64KiB bounds; artifact overflow), 1304/1322 (resume UNSUPPORTED; runtime-pinned Claude only). Landed surfaces: runner scaffold committed (canonical.ts sha256Hex/canonicalDigest for digest re-verification); skills exact shapes (skill-snapshot.ts:44-49, skill-loader.ts:29-34, skill-contract.ts:9); testkit canonicalize/identifyEvidence for fixture pins; .gitattributes eol=lf forces base64 for CRLF-bearing raw fixtures (a \r\n fixture in a text file would be silently corrupted). External effect supervisor (task-312c1de3) hard-depends on this task and owns supervisor/** — fence enumerated in step 1. This task unblocks the Codex adapter (task-a0fa6da4, BLOCKED naming this as needsFrom).
planningNotes.risks: (1) Authority laundering through render output or a hostile snapshot is the security-critical surface — type-level impossibility + runtime refusal + red-team walk. (2) Capability optimism: help text / version strings are not proof — every capability needs a method-of-proof record or UNSUPPORTED. (3) Fixture byte fidelity: base64-only raw payloads; the \r\n round-trip check post-commit catches gitattributes surprises. (4) Boundary creep into supervisor territory (process control, ARMED/SUSPECT, pinning execution) — grep-enforced fence; QA should reject any child_process import. (5) Unknown-schema vs capability-changed conflation would corrupt reconciliation semantics downstream — distinct outcomes tested. (6) Inline-retention bound: over-limit streams must produce the artifact-ref outcome while digest coverage stays complete — dedicated red-team case. (7) Shared tree: Clean-workspace steps 5-7 continue in disjoint runner paths; foreign-red attribution at the repo gate; 10-path explicit commit.
